questions.question: How does a {org} npm package get published, and why does the release job compare the git tag with package.json first?
questions.gold: A GitHub Actions workflow on a v* tag runs npm publish --provenance through npm Trusted Publishing over OIDC, with no NPM_TOKEN secret (only the very first publish of a new name uses a short-lived token). The job fails before publishing when the tag and the committed package.json version disagree, because v0.5.0 through v0.7.0 once published nothing for nine weeks while npm's duplicate-version rejection read like an auth failure.

questions.question: How does Lore's web UI receive live run updates and plan collaboration traffic?
questions.gold: Over one WebSocket per browser tab at lore-api's /api/ws, multiplexed into channels (run, runs, plan) with a JSON envelope. It replaced one SSE connection per run.

questions.question: Where do Lore's agent pods run, and does Lore hold a Kubernetes client to start them?
questions.gold: They run in pods of the external floor ({org}/floor), which Lore reaches only through @{org}/floor-client (FLOOR_API_URL). Lore holds no Kubernetes client.

questions.question: How are Lore's service metrics collected and viewed?
questions.gold: Each service exposes Prometheus text on a metrics port (:9464) through OpenTelemetry. kube-prometheus-stack (terraform enable_monitoring) scrapes it and Grafana shows it. Traces go to Cloud Trace, from lore-api only.

questions.question: If pushing a spec to Utopia fails during a Lore ingest, does the ingest fail?
questions.gold: No. Utopia is a mirror. A failed push is logged and counted (lore_utopia_mirror_failures_total) and never fails the ingest.

questions.question: What makes Lore's auto-merge loop keep waiting instead of approving a pull request?
questions.gold: Any of these holds the wait. Red CI, a merge conflict, an open review thread, a review not yet approved on the head commit, or the pull request being younger than auto_merge.min_age_hours (24 by default).

questions.question: In Lore, after a push to main, how many implementation-loop upkeep runs can start per repository, and which pull requests go first?
questions.gold: At most 3 per event per repository. The pull request upkept longest ago goes first. That is one never upkept, then the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, then the oldest.

questions.question: Which Lore loops run on a repository whose settings say nothing about them?
questions.gold: Triage, spec upkeep and spec tickets are on by omission. The implementation loop, code review (auto_review), auto-merge and digest are off by omission.

questions.question: What does Lore strip from memories and episodes before storing them?
questions.gold: API keys, JWTs, private keys, connection strings and bearer tokens, removed by sanitizeContent()/redactSecrets().

questions.question: What must a Lore skill's SKILL.md contain for the pull request check to pass?
questions.gold: A Help block fenced by <!-- lore-help:begin --> and <!-- lore-help:end --> holding a **Summary.** and a **Usage:**. The skill-help check (scripts/check-skill-help.sh) fails a skill without one.

questions.question: In Lore, which file decides whether a pull request is ready for the auto-merge loop to approve?
questions.gold: apps/stations/src/work/pr-ready-check/decide-merge-ready.ts, with its reads in merge-readers.ts beside it.

questions.question: Where is the Lore-Task footer of Lore-authored pull request bodies composed?
questions.gold: prFooter() in libs/shared/src/domain/pr-body.ts.

questions.question: Which Lore function puts a GitHub issue into a repository's implementation backlog?
questions.gold: queueTicket in libs/shared/src/work/backlog/queue-ticket.ts. It applies to an issue with a priority:* label, which a lore or lore:implementation label also gives.

questions.question: Where is the similarity threshold that marks two Lore memory facts as contradicting defined, and what is its value?
questions.gold: 0.92, defined twice: FACT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.92 in libs/shared/src/outbound/dgraph-fact-contradictions.ts, and in libs/server-core/src/work/memory/fact-contradictions.ts read from the LORE_FACT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD env var with 0.92 as its default. Either location is right.

questions.question: When was Lore's own Floor engine (apps/floor) deleted, and what replaced it?
questions.gold: On 2026-10-02 in commit ca031776d (#2431). The external floor ({org}/floor, ADR-049) replaced it.

questions.question: When was Lore's nightly context reindex job retired?
When was Lore's event-router deleted, and what now receives GitHub webhooks?
questions.gold: It was deleted when PR #2491 merged on 2026-10-02 at 22:13 UTC (commit 6682f8999, dated 2026-10-03 00:13 in CEST; either date is right). lore-api's POST /api/webhook/github receives the webhooks and writes pipeline.events.

questions.question: When did Lore's context reads become able to choose between Lore's own stores and Utopia?
questions.gold: On 2026-10-16, by PR #2787 ("Context reads choose a backend: lore, utopia or both"; merge commit 5b157bdfc, also on main as fb53a29c0; either commit is right), which added backend lore | utopia | both.

questions.question: Which Lore pull request moved the implementation loop's fix-ci step to Gemini 4 Argon?
Which Lore issue tracks retiring Dgraph by mirroring the code-to-spec graph into Utopia?
questions.gold: #2766, "Retire Dgraph: mirror the code-to-spec graph in Utopia, slice 1".

questions.question: Which Lore pull request added the spec tickets loop to the Loops tab?
Which Lore pull request stopped the context evals from running on a schedule?
questions.gold: #2823, merged 2026-10-19 ("run from a developer machine, never on a schedule").

questions.question: In Lore, why can an OpenTelemetry instrument created at module import never record anything?
questions.gold: The OTel metrics API has no proxy meter. An instrument created before the SDK registers its meter provider stays a no-op for good, so Lore resolves its instruments lazily against the current provider.

questions.question: Why did Lore's Gemini agent pods before 2026-09-23 run with no MCP tools?
questions.gold: ai-agent-subsystem v0.11.2 wrote the MCP servers into a system-scope settings file, which gemini-cli refuses for a uid-1000 directory. v0.11.3 writes them to the user settings (/agent/.gemini/settings.json).

questions.question: Why does Lore's weekly Utopia backfill sweep call lore-api over node:http rather than fetch?
questions.gold: fetch gives up after 5 minutes without response headers, and a backfill takes longer. The sweep uses node:http with a 30-minute wait.

questions.question: Must Lore's code review run on a different model family from the implementer?
questions.gold: No. ADR-039 proposed cross-family review but is still a draft, so it was never a rule. Its 2026-10-14 amendment put code-review and code-review-recheck on gemini-4-argon, the implementation loop's own family, because it caught more, so cross-family is only one input to the model choice.

questions.question: Does Lore's auto-merge loop fix a pull request whose CI is red?
questions.gold: No. It did when it shipped (#3320, 2026-10-23), but #3376 the same day removed the fix agent ("auto merge fixes nothing"). A loop pull request is repaired by the implementation loop's upkeep run, and a person's pull request by the person.

questions.question: Do Lore's context evals run nightly in CI?
questions.gold: No. They ran nightly from 2026-10-02 (#2463) until #2823 (2026-10-19) removed the schedule. They now run from a developer machine.

questions.question: What p99 latency SLO is defined for Lore's /api/context route?
questions.gold: None. No SLO or p99 latency target is defined anywhere for /api/context.

questions.question: Who is the PagerDuty on-call owner for lore-api?
questions.gold: Unknown. No on-call owner is recorded in the repository, its docs or its tracker.
